news.title: British Council moots axing 25% of workforce to pay off pandemic loan
news.summary_en: The British Council is considering further layoffs to help pay off a £197 million government bailout, an investigation from the National Audit Office (NAO) has revealed.
news.author: Beth Kennedy

news.title: QS rankings: US loses ground on research and talent attraction
news.summary_en: While America remains the frontrunner on graduate employability, its universities are losing ground to rivals in China and beyond as the research gap and international talent race tighten.
news.author: Polly Nash

news.title: India’s university rise broadens beyond IITs, but internationalisation lags
news.summary_en: More than half of India's ranked universities improved their position in the QS World University Rankings 2027, with 18 institutions reaching record highs as gains spread beyond the IITs despite persistent internationalisation challenges.
news.author: Abhishek Nair

news.title: Acumen acquires EduCorePro to boost AI-driven enrolment transformation
news.summary_en: Acumen has announced the acquisition of EduCorePro, an AI-enabled admissions technology company, in a move aimed at accelerating the transformation of global student recruitment and enrolment services through AI.
news.author: Kim Martin

news.title: The Netherlands records first-ever international student drop
news.summary_en: The total number of international students in The Netherlands has dropped for the first time since records began 20 years ago, new Nuffic data has shown.
news.author: Polly Nash

news.title: Ofqual fines Cambridge English £875k over IELTS marking errors
news.summary_en: UK qualifications regulator Ofqual has fined Cambridge English £875,000 following an investigation into automated marking errors that led to incorrect IELTS results being issued to more than 62,000 learners worldwide between 2023 and 2025.
news.author: Kim Martin

news.title: One Nation seeks crackdown on student visa “course-hopping”
news.summary_en: Right-wing Australian senator Pauline Hanson has reignited debate over international students, calling for tougher visa rules that would force students to leave the country before reapplying to study.
news.author: Kim Martin

news.title: Nigerian agents report extortion over deposits kept by UK unis
news.summary_en: The PIE understands that agents are having to “bail out” colleagues and sub-agents in Nigeria who are being arrested or extorted over tuition fee deposits being withheld by British universities.
news.author: Nicholas Cuthbert

news.title: 98% of leaders say study abroad shaped their path to leadership
news.summary_en: US industry leaders have reported that international educational experiences acted as a long-term accelerator for leadership, as stakeholders call for a broadening of how we talk about study abroad opportunities.
news.author: Polly Nash

news.title: Nigeria lifts tuition remittance cap even as visa concerns persist
news.summary_en: The Central Bank of Nigeria has increased the maximum tuition fee remittance for students studying abroad from $15,000 to $25,000 per semester, though experts say access to visas and funding remains a greater concern for many prospective students.
news.author: Abhishek Nair
